prerequisites: Knowledge of concepts addressed in courses of electronics, controls, electronic calculators and fundamentals of computer science.

learning_outcomes.text: Identify and choose the main components making up a chain of measurement acquisition of the conditions of an industrial process.
Intervene on the process by means of an electromechanical actuator to maintain the stability of the process, that is operation within desired minimum conditions.
Apply microprocessor control identified within a series of known algorithms and techniques.

syllabus_topics: Electronic chain of acquisition and control
Transducers for measuring linear and angular position
Transducers for measuring linear and angular velocity
Transducers for measuring level and acidity
The use of operational amplifiers in measurement chains: amplification with diode and single and double half-wave AC-DC converter
Creation of a circuit for the analog-digital set point
Resumption of proportional, proportional-integral and proportional-integral-derivative control
Examples of process acquisition and control chains in typical applications of the automation world
assessment_rules: The written test will contain an example of an industrial process where students must identify the correct transducer, the transfer function of the process, and the control algorithm needed for stabilization. The second part of the test focuses on describing a transducer and its conditioning electronics or an actuator. The test concludes with short questions requiring identification of reasons for behaviors of transducers, electronic circuits, control techniques, and actuators.
